l.t: Isuzuma risoza icyumweru n'imyitozo nzamurab ushobozi na nyagurab ushobozi

-Igitabo cy’umwarimu,
-Igitabo cy'umunyeshuri; ●Integanyanyigisho: Ikiciro cya mbere cy'amashuri abanza, Kigali.

l.o:

l.c: ●Ibibazo by'isuzum a.

●Igitabo cy’umunyeshuri, igitabo cy’umwarimu; ●Umwarimu ashaka n’izindi mfashanyigisho zifatika n’izidafatika zijyanye n’iri somo ziboneka aho ishuri riherereye.

●REB, 2026, Ikinyarwanda, Amashuri abanza 1,
-Igitabo cy’umwarimu,
-Igitabo cy'umunyeshuri; ●Integanyanyigisho: Ikiciro cya mbere cy'amashuri abanza, Kigali.

l.o: Identify key words for greetings and farewells and practise them in dialogue
l.c: Good morning, hello, hi, how are you? good afternoon, good evening, good night, see you tomorrow
l.a: The teacher greets learners with “Good morning!” and models responses. Pupils repeat greetings and practice greetings in pairs. Pupils use time-of-day visuals (Eg: flash cards, drawing on the chalk board or pictures in the student book) to match greetings to morning, afternoon, evening or night scenes, orally Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences. Teacher say the sentence; pupils clap on each word they hear then they say the number. E.g: Good morning teacher. (3 words), Good night everyone! (3 words.
l.m: Greetings and farewells pictures/ch arts/poster s, flash cards based on time: sunrise, noon, sunset and night
l.e: Pupils produce greeting phrases correctly in role-play and in conversation. Teacher checks both accuracy and appropriateness of the greetings
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book. (2023)

l.t: Practice greetings and farewells through short dialogues
l.o: Use greetings and farewells appropriately in short dialogues
l.c: Good morning, how are, hello, hi, good afternoon, good evening, good night, see you tomorrow
l.a: Teacher models mini-dialogues. Eg: Teacher: “Good morning!” Pupil: “Good morning!” Visual prompts: Teacher shows a picture (sunrise, bright sun in the sky, sunset, nigt (moon and stars) and pupils act out the matching dialogue. Practice greetings: Half the class greets, the other half responds, then they switch roles. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences.
l.m: Greetings/farewells pictures and flash cards Pictures of sunrise, noon, sunset, and night
l.e: The teacher checks accuracy of the greetings & farewells’ responses and whether pupils can recall the correct phrase for the time of day.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book. (2023)

l.t: Practice greetings and farewells through short role-play situations
l.o: Use greetings and farewells appropriately in short role-play based on context (time & people)
l.c: Good afternoon, good evening, good night, hello teacher, hello friend
l.a: In small groups, pupils match greetings to pictures of sunrise, noon, sunset, and night orally Role play: Practice greeting a teacher, a friend, or a visitor using appropriate simple phrases (from student book). Pupils move around greeting classmates using the correct time-of-day phrases Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences.
l.m: Pictures of sunrise, noon, sunset, and night
l.e: Teacher observes fluency, confidence, and whether pupils choose greetings that fit the situation.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book. (2023)

l.o:
Listen to the story “Hello” read out aloud, identify key words on greetings and make
sentences using them
l.c: Good morning, hello, how are you? Good afternoon, good night, see you tomorrow!
l.a:
Before reading: Pupils make predictions through the title or the pictures of the story “Hello” During reading: Read aloud for the first time while asking questions and exploring new words (Eg: good morning, good afternoon, good night, my name is, etc.) Conduct a second read aloud from the beginning to the end without stopping.
After reading: Ask pupils if their predictions become true. Pupils respond to comprehension questions in the book and encourage pupils to respond based on what they heard from the story “Hello”. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in sentences from the story.
l.m: Story “Hello”
l.e: Teacher checks for accuracy in using new words and responding accurately to comprehension questions
l.r: P1 term 1 read aloud story book page 1-4

l.o: Re-listen to the story “Hello” read out aloud and respond to related comprehension questions
l.c: See above
l.a: During this lesson. The teacher re-reads the story aloud following the read aloud steps but puts much focus on areas where pupils need support. Before reading: Teacher prompts pupils to recall the main events of the story “Hello”. Eg: What happened at the beginning, middle or end? During reading: Teacher re- read aloud the story “Hello” from the beginning to the end without stopping. After reading: Ask comprehension questions. Ask pupils an additional question to connect the story to their real life experience. (eg: When do you eat lunch ?) Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in other sentences from the story.
l.m: Story “Hello”
l.e: Teacher checks for accuracy and confidence in responding to questions and retelling the story
l.r: P1 term 1 read aloud story book page 1-4

l.o: Identify key words for self-introduction and use them correctly
l.c: My name is …, What is your name?, I am …, I am new here, What’s your name again?
l.a: Teacher models: “My name is ….” Using gestures. Pupils repeat. Teacher practices the greetings dialogue (from pupil book) with one pupil. Pair practice: pupils introduce themselves. and practice the dialogue with the guidance of the teacher. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences. E.g: What is your name? (4 words) My name is Keza. (4 words), Who is this? (3 words).
l.m: Name tags, flashcards, posters
l.e: Pupils use self-introduction phrases correctly in conversations. Teacher checks accuracy and appropriateness
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (2023)

l.o: Use self-introduction phrases appropriately in short dialogues
l.c: See above
l.a: Teacher models mini-dialogues (from student book): Teacher: “Hello, my name is ….” What is your name? Pupil: My name is ….. Teacher: Nice to meet you! Dialogue: Pupils practice introducing oneself in pairs with gestures. Mingle mingle: One greet and introduce him/herself, the other responds, they switch then mingle mingle again to find another partner. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences.
l.m: Flash cards, pictures
l.e: The teacher checks the accuracy of introductions and whether pupils recall the correct phrases.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book 2023)

l.o: Use self-introduction phrases in short role-play situations
l.c: See above
l.a: Role play: pupils practice meeting a new classmate and introduce themselves with the correct phrases. Repeat this as many times as possible. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences.
l.m: Pictures
l.e: Teacher observes fluency, confidence, and whether pupils choose phrases that fit the situation.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book, 2023

l.o: Listen to the story “I am Keza”, identify key words, and use them to make sentences
l.c: Hello, what is your name? My name is …, Nice to meet you! You are welcome!
l.a: Before reading: Pupils make predictions from title/pictures. During reading: teacher reads aloud “I am Keza”, pausing to ask questions for pupils to explore key words. The teacher read a second time from the beginning to the end without stopping to reinforce the pupil's comprehension. After reading: Teachers checks pupils’ predictions and have them respond to comprehension questions. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in sentences from the story.
l.m: Story “I am Keza”
l.e: Teacher checks for accuracy in using new words and responding accurately to comprehension questions
l.r: P1 Term 1 Read Aloud Story Book, page 5 to 8

l.o: Re-listen to “I am Keza” and respond to related comprehension questions
l.c: See above
l.a: During this lesson. The teacher re-reads the story aloud following the read aloud steps but puts much focus on areas where pupils need support. Before reading: teacher prompts pupils to recall main events of I am Keza story. During reading: teacher re-reads aloud without stopping. After reading: pupils answer comprehension questions orally. Teacher ask pupils an additional question to connect the story to their real life experience. (What is the name of this girl? Point to one girl in your classroom.) Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in other sentences from the story.
l.m: Storybook I am Keza
l.e: Teacher checks for accuracy and confidence in responding to questions and retelling the story
l.r: P1 Term 1 Read Aloud Story, page 5 to 8

l.o: Identify key words for introducing others and use them correctly
l.c: Who is this?, This is …, Who is that?, That is …, He is …, She is …, They are …, This is my friend, She is my classmate
l.a: Teacher models: “Who is this? This is my friend.” Pupils repeat. Pair practice: pupils introduce classmates using names and gestures. Pupils use visuals (eg: pictures in the student book) to match phrases orally. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences. E.g: This is my friend Kalisa. (5 words) She is my classmate. (4 words)
l.m: Name tags, flashcards, posters
l.e: Pupils use introduction phrases correctly in conversations. The teacher checks accuracy and appropriateness
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (2023)

l.t: Practice introducing others through short dialogues
l.o: Use introduction phrases appropriately in short dialogues
l.c: See above
l.a: Teacher prompts pupils with questions to enable them introduce their colleagues. Eg: Teacher: “Who is this?” → Pupil: “This is my friend. He is Peter.” Dialogue: Pupils practice introducing others in pairs. Mingle mingle: Pupils walk around, introduce themselves, introduce a classmate, then switch partners as many times as possible. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences.
l.m: Flashcards, pictures
l.e: The teacher checks accuracy of introductions and whether pupils recall the correct phrases.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (2023)

l.t: Practice introducing others through role play
l.o: Use introduction phrases in short role-play situations
l.c: See above
l.a: Role play: pupils practice introducing a friend to the teacher or visitor using the correct phrases. Repeat several times for fluency. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences
l.m: P1 Pupil’s English Book pictures
l.e: Teacher observes fluency, confidence, and whether pupils choose phrases
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book 2023)

l.o: Listen to the story I am Keza, identify key words, and use them to make sentences
l.c: Hello, what is your name? My name is …, Nice to meet you! Who is this? This is …, You are welcome!
l.a: Before reading: Pupils share what they remember about the story “I am Keza”. During reading: teacher re-reads I am Keza, pausing to highlight key words related to introducing others. Teacher reads a second time continuously without stopping. After reading: The teacher checks pupils’ predictions and have them respond to comprehension questions. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in sentences from the story.
l.m: Story I am Keza
l.e: Teacher checks for accuracy in using new words and responding accurately to comprehension questions
l.r: P1 Term 1 Read Aloud Story Book (pp. 5–8)

l.o: Re-listen to I am Keza and respond to related comprehension questions
l.c: See above
l.a: Before reading: recall main events of I am Keza. Teacher shows pictures from the story in order, pupils say what is happening on each of them. During reading: teacher re-reads aloud without stopping from the beginning to the end. After reading: pupils answer comprehension questions orally. Teacher asks additional questions to help pupils connect the story with their every day’s life. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in other sentences from the story.
l.m: Story I am Keza
l.e: Teacher checks for accuracy and confidence in responding to questions and retelling the story .
l.r: P1 Term 1 Read Aloud Story Book (pp. 5–8)

l.o: Identify key words for classroom instructions and use them correctly
l.c: Clap, stamp, sit, stand, sing, point, raise your hand, look at the board, listen carefully, point to …
l.a: Teacher models: “Clap your hands,” “Sit down.” Pupils repeat and act out. Pair practice: One pupil gives the instruction, the other on do actions. Pupils use P1 Pupil’s English Book visuals to match actions. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences. E.g: Sit down! (2 words), Open the door. (3 words) Sing the song. (3 words)
l.m: Flashcards, posters, classroom objects
l.e: Pupils follow and give instructions correctly. Teacher checks accuracy and appropriateness
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (2023)

l.t: Practice instructions through dialogue and role play
l.o: Use instruction phrases appropriately in short dialogues and role-play situations
l.c: See above
l.a: Teacher models mini-dialogues: Teacher: “clap your hands.” Pupil: “Yes, teacher.” Pupils practice in pairs using dialogue visuals. Role play: Pupils act out classroom routines (teacher gives instructions; pupils follow). Use real classroom props (board, books, chairs). Repeat several times for fluency. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences.
l.m: Flashcards, pictures, real classroom objects
l.e: Teacher checks accuracy of instructions and observes fluency, confidence, and whether pupils follow instructions correctly.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (2023)

l.t: Read aloud story “Do as I say”
l.o: Listen to the story “Do as I say”, identify key words, and use them to make sentences
l.c: Stand up, listen, go play, sing, jump
l.a:
Before reading: Pupils predict what will happen in the story “Do as I say” from the title/pictures. During reading: teacher reads aloud the story “Do as I say”, pausing to highlight key words and help pupils understand them. The teacher reads a second time continuously.
After reading: Teacher checks pupils’ predictions and have them respond to comprehension questions. Phonological awareness: Pupil count the words in sentences from the story.
l.m: Story Do as I say
l.e:
Teacher checks for accuracy in using new words and responding accurately to
comprehension questions
l.r: P1 Term 1 Read Aloud Story Book (pp. 9–12)

l.t: Re-read aloud story “Do as I say”
l.o: Re-listen to Do as I say and respond to related comprehension questions
l.c: See above
l.a: Before reading: pupils recall the main events of the story “Do as I say” based on the pictures or prompts questions from the teacher. During reading: teacher re-reads aloud without stopping. After reading: pupils answer comprehension questions orally. Phonological awareness: Count the words in other sentences from the story.
l.m: Story Do as I say
l.e: Teacher checks for accuracy and confidence in responding to questions and retelling the story
l.r: P1 Term 1 Read Aloud Story Book (pp. 9–12)

l.o: Demonstrate competence in greetings, introductions , and classroom instructions
l.c: See key words from week 1 to 4: Greetings, self-introduction, introducing others, classroom instructions
l.a:
Teacher conducts oral assessment. Eg:
 Pupils greet, introduce themselves and others, and follow classroom instructions from the teacher.
 Role-play scenarios: greeting a friend, introducing a classmate, following colleagues’ commands.
 Look at the picture for sunrise, noon, sunset, night, and say the right greetings.
l.m: Flashcards, posters, classroom objects
l.e: Pupils demonstrate mastery of Unit 1 skills: greetings, introductions, and instructions. The teacher records the performance of each pupil.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (Unit 1 review)

u.k: Pupils communicate appropriately through greetings, introductions and classroom routines, and respond meaningfully to theme-based read-aloud stories.

l.o: Identify and name classroom objects using demonstratives
l.c: What is this?, What is that?, It is …, These are … (desk, pencil, window, blackboard, book, cupboard, duster, notebook, pen, rubber, chair, sharpener)
l.a: Teacher models: “What is this? It is a desk.” Pupils repeat. Pair practice: pupils point to real classroom items and name them. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences. E.g: This is my classroom. (4 words), I have a book. (4 words)
l.m: Real classroom items, flashcards, posters
l.e: Pupils identify and name classroom objects correctly using demonstratives. Teacher checks accuracy.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (2023)

l.t: Practice describing classroom objects through short dialogues
l.o: Use simple sentences to describe classroom items
l.c: See above
l.a: Teacher models mini-dialogues (from student book): Teacher: “What is this?” → Pupil: “It is a desk” Pupils practice naming classroom objects in pairs using P1 Pupil’s English Book visuals or real objects. Mingle mingle: Pupils walk around, ask “What is this?” and respond with “It is …” or “These are ….” They repeat with as many classroom objects as possible
l.m: Real classroom objects, flash cards
l.e: Teacher checks accuracy of dialogues and whether pupils recall the correct phrases.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (20238)

l.t: Practice describing classroom objects through role play
l.o: Use classroom vocabulary in short role-play situations
l.c: See above
l.a: Role play: pupils act out classroom scenes (teacher asks “What is this?” pupils respond “It is a pen”). In small groups, pupils identify classroom items (books, pens, rulers) and present them to the class. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences.
l.m: Real classroom objects, flash cards
l.e: Teacher observes fluency, confidence, and whether pupils use correct demonstratives.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (2023)

l.o: Listen to the story Sano’s classroom, identify key words, and use them to make sentences
l.c: Chair, desk, school bag, notebook, pen, rubber, pencil, blackboard
l.a: Before reading: Pupils predict what the story “Sano’s classroom” will be about from the title/pictures. During reading: teacher reads aloud the story Sano’s classroom, pausing to highlight key words. Teacher reads a second time continuously up to the end. After reading: Pupils check predictions and respond to comprehension questions Phonological awareness: Count the words in sentences from the story.
l.m: Story Sano’s classroom
l.e: Teacher checks for accuracy in using new words and responding accurately to comprehension questions
l.r: P1 Term 1 Read Aloud Story Book (page 13– 16)

l.o:
Re-listen to Sano’s classroom and respond to
related comprehension questions
l.c: See above
l.a:
Before reading: Teacher prompts pupils to recall main events of Sano’s classroom.
During reading: teacher re-reads aloud without stopping. After reading: pupils answer comprehension questions orally. Ask pupils an additional question to connect the story to their real life experience. (e.g: what classroom materials do you like?) Phonological awareness: Count the words in other sentences from the story.
l.m: Story Sano’s classroom
l.e:
Teacher checks for accuracy and confidence in
responding to questions and retelling the story
l.r:
P1 Term 1 Read Aloud
Story Book (page 15– 18)

l.o: Identify and name colours using classroom vocabulary
l.c: Blue, yellow, white, red, black, green, indigo, orange, violet, brown, purple, pink, grey, what colour is this pen? It is blue. What colour is the ruler? It is yellow. What colour are these books? They are white.
l.a: Teacher models naming colours: “What colour is this pen? It is blue.” Pupils repeat. Pair practice: pupils point to classroom items and name their colours. Pupils name objects and identify an object with different colour Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences. . E.g: My ruler is blue. (4 words), Here is my school bag. (5 words)
l.m: Colour flashcards, classroom items with different colours
l.e: Pupils identify and name colours correctly using classroom vocabulary. The teacher checks accuracy.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (2023)

l.o: Use colour words in simple sentences
l.c: Same as above
l.a: Teacher models mini-dialogues: Teacher: “What colour is this pen?” → Pupil: “It is red.” Pupils practice naming colours of practice objects in pairs using pictures in the pupil book. Mingle mingle: Pupils walk around asking and answering colour questions with partners. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences.
l.m: Coloured objects, sentence strips
l.e: Teacher checks accuracy of dialogues and whether pupils recall the correct colour phrases.
l.r: P1 Pupil’s English Book (2023)

l.o: Use colour vocabulary in short role-play situations
l.c: Same as above

Teacher models: “This is my book.” Pupils repeat. Pair practice: pupils point to classroom items in class or on flash cards and say “This is my …” or “That is her ….”
Pupils pick classroom objects and match them with owners. Eg: This is Jane’s bag. It is her school bag. Phonological awareness: Pupils count the words in familiar songs or sentences. E.g: I have 2 books and 2 pens. (7 words), Do you have a ruler? (5 words)

Pupils identify and respond to possessive phrases using correct pronouns and vocabulary.
Teacher checks accuracy.

Phonological awareness: Teacher say words. Pupils find words that rhyme (sound the same at the end) with each word. E.g: beginning/evening, end/bend, pen/hen; halls/walls Alphabetic awareness: Teacher introduces letter f/F. Pupils practice saying names and writing lowercase and uppercase forms.

l.a:
The teacher models how to identify the story sequence markers. The teacher tells a simple story to pupils orally. She/he stresses on the story markers (Eg: once upon a time, after, then, etc.). Teacher asks: What word did I use to start the story? What other words did I use to connect main parts in my story? Which word did I use to mark the end of my story? Pupils respond. Teachers support where necessary. Pair practice: Pupils retell the story from the teacher using the story connectors/story sequence markers.
Phonological awareness: Teacher say words. Pupils find words that rhyme (sound the same at the end) with each word. E.g: ending/beginning, cat/hat, sun/fun, dog, log Alphabetic awareness: Teacher introduces letters x/X. Pupils practice saying names and writing lowercase and uppercase forms. Demonstrate how to form this letter as this is the first time for pupils to learn them as they don’t exist in Kinyarwanda. Pupils read x/X.

l.e: The teacher observes fluency, confidence, and whether pupils use correct story vocabulary.

-Learners observe the pictures and discuss the questions on introductory activity 1.0 in pupil’s book.
l.m: Mathematics book, real-life objects with numbers (e.g., calendar, clock), chalk/whiteboard etc

l.o: Count objects up to 2 accurately.

l.r: Mathematic s book for Primary one (Page1 -2)

l.o: Read, and write the number 1.

l.a: 1. Teacher shows flashcard with the number '1'. 2. Pupils practice writing '1' in the air, on their desks, and in their exercise books. 3. Activity: Draw one object (e.g., one sun, one tree, one cow, one pineapple, etc). Notice: Adapt activities so that pupils with special education needs, can participate.
l.m: Number flashcard (1), chalkboard, exercise books, pencils, Etc,
l.e: Pupils should be given written sheet and practical on activities Reading and writing the number 1.

l.a: 1. Revise number 1. Introduce flashcard for number 2. 2. Pupils practice writing numbers 1 and 2. 3. Matching game: Match cards with '1' to a picture of one apple; '2' to two bananas. Notice: Adapt activities so that pupils with special education needs, can participate.
l.m: Number flashcards (1 & 2), picture cards with 1 and 2 objects, exercise books, pencils, pens, etc.

l.a: 1. Sing a counting song up to 3 (e.g., "One, Two, Buckle My Shoe", etc). 2. Teacher uses bottle tops/beans to demonstrate counting to 3. 3. Pupils work in pairs: one pupil places a number of objects for instance three avocadoes,

l.a: 1. In pair, pupils write numbers 1 and 2. 2. Introduce number 3 with a flashcard. 3. Tracing activity: Pupils trace numbers 1, 2, and 3 in their books. 4. Game: "Show me..." Teacher says a number, pupils hold up the correct number of fingers.
l.m: Number flashcards (1,2,3), tracing worksheets, pencils
l.e: Pupils should be given a Worksheet completion and practical activities on Reading and writing the numbers 1, 2, and 3
l.r: Mathematic s book for Primary one (Page 4)

l.o: Count objects up to 4 accurately.
l.c: count One, Count two, Count three, Count four
l.a: 1. Count pupils in a row (up to 4). 2. Use a number line to point and count from 1 to 4. 3. Activity: Count and Say the number of fishes, carrots

l.e: Pupils should be given oral questions and practical demonstration activities on Counting 1 to 4 objects.

l.o: Count objects up to 5 accurately.

l.a: 1. Use a familiar song (e.g "Five Little Monkeys") to count to 5. 2. Count body parts: 1 nose, 2 eyes, 5 fingers on one hand. 3. Practical task: Count out 5 beans into a cup then

l.m: Flashcards, worksheets, pencils
l.e: Pupils should be given guided writing practice and Worksheet activities on Reading and writing the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5

l.t: Comparing numbers of 5 or fewer than 5 objects
l.o: Compare two groups of objects and use the terms "more than", "less than", and "equal to".
l.c: Use More, less, same number, is greater than (>), is less than(<), is equal to (=).
l.a: 1. Use two groups of bottles tops. Ask: "Which group has more?" 2. Introduce vocabulary: “more than, less than”. 3. Pair work: Pupils create two groups with counters and compare them.
l.m: Counters, bottles tops, objects of different quantities
l.e: Pupils should be given oral questions, and practical activities on Comparing numbers of 5 or fewer than 5 objects
l.r: Mathematic s book for Primary one (Page 9-12)

l.t: Ascending order of numbers from 1 to 5
l.o: Arrange numbers from the smallest to the biggest (1 to 5).
l.c: Ascending order, smaller, bigger, biggest, first, next, last.
l.a: 1. Use a number line to show the order from 1 to 5. 2. Pupils line up in order based on number cards they are holding. 3. Worksheet: Write numbers 1-5 in ascending order.
l.m: Number line, number cards, worksheet, etc
l.e: Pupils should be given oral presentations, written and practical activities on arranging numbers up to 5 from the smallest to the biggest.
l.r: Mathematic s book for Primary one (Page 13)

l.t: Descending order of numbers from 1 to 5
l.o:
Arrange numbers from the biggest to the
smallest (5 to 1).
l.c: Descending order, big, smaller, smallest
l.a:
1. Use the number line to count backwards: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.
2. Game: "Number Jump" - Place number cards on the floor. Pupils jump from 5 to 1. 3. Worksheet: Write numbers 5-1 in descending order.
l.m:
Number line, number cards, worksheet,
real objects.
l.e:
Pupils should be given oral presentations, written and
practical activities on arranging numbers up to 5 from the biggest to the smallest.
l.r: Mathematic s book for Primary one (Page 13)

l.t: Addition of numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 5
l.o: Combine two groups of objects and find the total (sum) up to 5.
l.c: Add numbers. Sign plus (+), Equals (=), total
l.a: 1. Use real objects: "I have 2 apples. You give me 1 more. How many do I have now?" 2. Introduce the '+' and '=' signs using flashcards. 3. Solve simple problems like 2 + 1 = ? using counters.
l.m: Counters, objects, addition sign flashcard, equals sign flashcard, Number cards
l.e: Pupils should be given Practical demonstration that Combine two groups of objects and find the total (sum) up to 5.
l.r: Mathematic s book for Primary one (Page 13-16)

l.t: Word problems on the addition of numbers whose sum does not exceed 5
l.o: Solve simple real-life word problems involving addition (sum ≤ 5).
l.c: Add, altogether, total
l.a:
1. Teacher tells a simple story: "Nadia had 2 sweets. Her mother gave her 2 more. How many does she have altogether?" 2. Use drawings on
the board to represent the story. 3. Pupils act out word problems using classmates. (e.g., 2 boys and 3 girls come to the board. How many children?)
l.m: Drawings on board, pupils themselves
l.e:
Pupils should be told model word problems stories on the addition of numbers whose sum
does not exceed 5.
l.r: Mathematic s book for Primary one (Page 17)

l.o: Find the difference between two groups of objects (up to 5) by taking away.
l.c: Subtract, take away, minus (-), left, remain
l.a: 1. Practical demonstration: "I have 4 books. I give 1 to Sarah. How many are left?" 2. Introduce the '-' sign using a flashcard.
l.m: Counters, books, subtraction sign flashcard
l.e: Pupils should be given practical activities Subtraction of numbers less than 5.
l.r: Mathematic s book for Primary one (Page18-20)

l.t: Word problem on subtraction of numbers less than 5
l.o: Solve simple real-life word problems involving subtraction (within 5).

l.m: Counters, drawings on board
l.e: Pupils should be given verbal subtraction problems on solving simple real-life word problems.
